name: FinOps for AI Lens
description: Canonical question, description, severity, remediation, maturity tier, and documentation URL per FinOps for AI check. Source: FinOps Foundation FinOps for AI working group asset library.

questions.title: Is there clear ownership and accountability for AI spending, with designated cost owners per team, project, or department?
questions.description: Clear ownership and accountability for AI spending is established — by team, project, or department.

choices.title: Is there clear ownership and accountability for AI spending, with designated cost owners per team, project, or department?

helpfulResource.displayText: Clear ownership and accountability for AI spending is established — by team, project, or department.

improvementPlan.displayText: Assign AI cost owners per team or project. Implement chargeback or showback models for AI spend. Include AI costs in team budget reviews.

questions.title: Are budget controls, spending quotas, and anomaly detection in place for AI workloads to prevent unexpected cost overruns?
questions.description: Budget controls, quotas, and anomaly detection are in place for AI spending to prevent unexpected cost overruns.

choices.title: Are budget controls, spending quotas, and anomaly detection in place for AI workloads to prevent unexpected cost overruns?

helpfulResource.displayText: Budget controls, quotas, and anomaly detection are in place for AI spending to prevent unexpected cost overruns.

improvementPlan.displayText: Set AWS Budgets with alerts for AI services. Implement per-team or per-project quotas. Enable Cost Anomaly Detection for AI service categories.

questions.title: Does AI cost forecasting account for optimization impacts, non-linear scaling, and the volatility of AI workload costs?
questions.description: AI cost forecasting accounts for the impact of optimization initiatives and the non-linear scaling characteristics of AI workloads.

choices.title: Does AI cost forecasting account for optimization impacts, non-linear scaling, and the volatility of AI workload costs?

helpfulResource.displayText: AI cost forecasting accounts for the impact of optimization initiatives and the non-linear scaling characteristics of AI workloads.

improvementPlan.displayText: Build AI-specific forecasting models that account for token volume growth, model changes, optimization savings, and seasonal usage patterns.

questions.title: Do AI projects use incremental funding with frequent review gates (fail-fast approach) rather than large upfront budget commitments?
questions.description: AI projects use incremental funding models with frequent fail-fast reviews rather than large upfront commitments.

choices.title: Do AI projects use incremental funding with frequent review gates (fail-fast approach) rather than large upfront budget commitments?

helpfulResource.displayText: AI projects use incremental funding models with frequent fail-fast reviews rather than large upfront commitments.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement stage-gated funding for AI projects: small initial budgets for experimentation, with incremental increases tied to demonstrated value.

questions.title: Have teams building and operating this AI solution received training on FinOps best practices specific to AI workloads (token economics, GPU optimization, cost attribution)?
questions.description: Teams building and operating AI solutions are trained on FinOps best practices specific to AI workloads.

choices.title: Have teams building and operating this AI solution received training on FinOps best practices specific to AI workloads (token economics, GPU optimization, cost attribution)?

helpfulResource.displayText: Teams building and operating AI solutions are trained on FinOps best practices specific to AI workloads.

improvementPlan.displayText: Provide AI-specific FinOps training covering token economics, GPU cost management, model selection trade-offs, and cost attribution practices.

questions.description: The AI model selected is appropriate for the task complexity. Smaller models are used for simple tasks, larger models reserved for complex reasoning.

helpfulResource.displayText: The AI model selected is appropriate for the task complexity. Smaller models are used for simple tasks, larger models reserved for complex reasoning.

improvementPlan.displayText: Benchmark smaller models (e.g., Haiku, Titan Lite) on representative queries. Use Bedrock Prompt Router to auto-route by complexity. Reserve large models for complex tasks.

questions.title: Are prompts optimized for token efficiency, including concise system prompts, controlled context windows, and max token limits on responses?
questions.description: Prompts are optimized for token efficiency — concise system prompts, minimal context window growth, and controlled response lengths.

choices.title: Are prompts optimized for token efficiency, including concise system prompts, controlled context windows, and max token limits on responses?

helpfulResource.displayText: Prompts are optimized for token efficiency — concise system prompts, minimal context window growth, and controlled response lengths.

improvementPlan.displayText: Audit system prompts for verbosity. Set max token limits on responses. Implement context window management to prevent creep over conversation turns.

questions.description: Prompt caching is enabled for repeated or similar prompts to reduce redundant token processing costs.

helpfulResource.displayText: Prompt caching is enabled for repeated or similar prompts to reduce redundant token processing costs.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable Bedrock prompt caching for system prompts and frequently repeated context. Monitor cache hit rates and cost savings.

questions.title: Are GPU and compute resources right-sized for AI workloads, with utilization monitored and idle resources addressed?
questions.description: GPU and compute resources are right-sized, with utilization monitored and idle resources identified and addressed.

choices.title: Are GPU and compute resources right-sized for AI workloads, with utilization monitored and idle resources addressed?

helpfulResource.displayText: GPU and compute resources are right-sized, with utilization monitored and idle resources identified and addressed.

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor GPU utilization (target >60%). Implement auto-scaling, spot instances for training, and scheduled scaling for predictable inference patterns.

questions.title: Is there a capacity commitment strategy in place, using provisioned throughput or reserved capacity where usage patterns justify it?
questions.description: A capacity commitment strategy is in place, transitioning from pay-as-you-go to provisioned capacity where usage patterns justify it.

choices.title: Is there a capacity commitment strategy in place, using provisioned throughput or reserved capacity where usage patterns justify it?

helpfulResource.displayText: A capacity commitment strategy is in place, transitioning from pay-as-you-go to provisioned capacity where usage patterns justify it.

improvementPlan.displayText: Analyze usage patterns to identify candidates for provisioned throughput. Treat capacity commitments as strategic decisions, not just discount mechanisms.

questions.title: Is the AI infrastructure model (fully managed like Bedrock, partially managed like SageMaker, or self-managed) aligned with the organization's FinOps maturity?
questions.description: The AI infrastructure model (fully managed, partially managed, or self-managed) is aligned with the organization's FinOps maturity and technical readiness.

choices.title: Is the AI infrastructure model (fully managed like Bedrock, partially managed like SageMaker, or self-managed) aligned with the organization's FinOps maturity?

helpfulResource.displayText: The AI infrastructure model (fully managed, partially managed, or self-managed) is aligned with the organization's FinOps maturity and technical readiness.

improvementPlan.displayText: Evaluate infrastructure choices against the Crawl/Walk/Run maturity model. Start with fully managed for experimentation, move to partially managed for scaling.

questions.description: Content pre-filtering or guardrails are used to block unnecessary or harmful requests before they consume model inference tokens.

helpfulResource.displayText: Content pre-filtering or guardrails are used to block unnecessary or harmful requests before they consume model inference tokens.

improvementPlan.displayText: Configure Bedrock Guardrails with content filters on input to block harmful or off-topic requests before they reach the model, saving inference costs.

questions.title: Are AI unit economics defined and tracked (e.g., cost per query, cost per transaction, cost per user, or cost per business outcome)?
questions.description: AI unit economics are defined and tracked (cost per query, cost per transaction, cost per user, or cost per business outcome).

choices.title: Are AI unit economics defined and tracked (e.g., cost per query, cost per transaction, cost per user, or cost per business outcome)?

helpfulResource.displayText: AI unit economics are defined and tracked (cost per query, cost per transaction, cost per user, or cost per business outcome).

improvementPlan.displayText: Define AI unit metrics aligned to business outcomes. Track cost-per-query, cost-per-conversation, or cost-per-resolution alongside business KPIs.

questions.title: Is the ROI of this AI solution measured against business value delivered, with metrics appropriate to its lifecycle stage?
questions.description: AI investments are measured against business value delivered, with clear ROI metrics at each lifecycle stage (concept, prototype, MVP, product).

choices.title: Is the ROI of this AI solution measured against business value delivered, with metrics appropriate to its lifecycle stage?

helpfulResource.displayText: AI investments are measured against business value delivered, with clear ROI metrics at each lifecycle stage (concept, prototype, MVP, product).

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement phased ROI measurement: market sizing at concept stage, value measurement at prototype, ROI evaluation at MVP, and TCO analysis at product stage.

questions.title: Is there a cross-functional AI Investment Council or governance body that aligns AI investments with strategic goals and reviews AI project value?
questions.description: A cross-functional AI Investment Council or equivalent governance body aligns AI investments with strategic goals and ethical standards.

choices.title: Is there a cross-functional AI Investment Council or governance body that aligns AI investments with strategic goals and reviews AI project value?

helpfulResource.displayText: A cross-functional AI Investment Council or equivalent governance body aligns AI investments with strategic goals and ethical standards.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish an AI Investment Council with representatives from engineering, finance, product, and compliance to review AI project portfolios and investment decisions.

questions.title: Are AI workload costs tracked with granular attribution (per team, project, model, or use case) using structured tagging?
questions.description: AI workloads are identified, tagged, and tracked with granular cost attribution (per team, project, model, or use case).

choices.title: Are AI workload costs tracked with granular attribution (per team, project, model, or use case) using structured tagging?

helpfulResource.displayText: AI workloads are identified, tagged, and tracked with granular cost attribution (per team, project, model, or use case).

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement structured tagging for all AI resources (e.g., AI_Project, AI_Team, AI_Model). Use AWS Cost Explorer or Cost and Usage Reports filtered by AI services.

questions.title: Is token consumption (input and output tokens) tracked per model, per application, and per team?
questions.description: Token consumption (input and output) is tracked per model, per application, and per user or team.

choices.title: Is token consumption (input and output tokens) tracked per model, per application, and per team?

helpfulResource.displayText: Token consumption (input and output) is tracked per model, per application, and per user or team.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable Bedrock model invocation logging to capture token usage. Build dashboards tracking input/output token ratios and costs per application.

questions.title: Is there a dedicated AI cost and usage tracking mechanism providing real-time or near-real-time visibility into AI spend?
questions.description: A dedicated AI cost and usage tracking mechanism is in place, providing real-time or near-real-time visibility into AI spend.

choices.title: Is there a dedicated AI cost and usage tracking mechanism providing real-time or near-real-time visibility into AI spend?

helpfulResource.displayText: A dedicated AI cost and usage tracking mechanism is in place, providing real-time or near-real-time visibility into AI spend.

improvementPlan.displayText: Build an AI cost tracker using Cost Explorer APIs, CloudWatch metrics, and invocation logs. Create dashboards with daily/weekly cost trends.

questions.title: Are AI workloads clearly identified and distinguished from non-AI workloads in cost reporting?

helpfulResource.displayText: AI workloads are identified and distinguished from non-AI workloads using a combination of known services, manual tagging, and discovery rules.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use a combination of service-based identification (Bedrock, SageMaker), resource tagging, and discovery rules to classify AI workloads.
